original_source: Duplicate email notifications from Jira Cloud and Atlassian Support Service Desk (getsupport.atlassian.com)
failure_pattern: A bug in the notification dispatch logic caused the system to send the same email twice for certain events, leading to duplicate notifications for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement idempotent notification dispatch; add de-duplication checks; add monitoring for duplicate events; add unit tests for notification logic; enforce code review for notification changes.

original_source: Partners Jira and Confluence access issues
symptoms: unable to log on to Jira
unable to log on to Confluence
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the authentication service caused partner users to be unable to log in to Jira and Confluence, resulting in access issues.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation; add health checks for authentication endpoints; monitor authentication logs; enforce strict change management and rollback procedures.

symptoms: intermittent failure connecting to Atlassian Cloud
failure_pattern: An increased DNS error rate from the infrastructure supplier caused intermittent DNS resolution failures, which in turn led to intermittent connectivity failures for some Atlassian Cloud customers.
mitigation_principle: 1. Monitor upstream DNS error rates and set alerts; 2. Implement redundant DNS resolvers; 3. Coordinate with suppliers for SLA and rapid issue resolution; 4. Deploy automated fallback to alternative DNS; 5. Conduct post-incident review and update incident response playbooks

original_source: Performance issues and outages with Cloud products
symptoms: slow loading and uploading of attachments
inability to sign up new customers
failure_pattern: An upgrade to a third‑party artifact management tool added new functionality that unexpectedly increased load on its primary database. The spike in database load degraded the scaling capabilities of the internal hosting platform, causing slow response times, feature outages, and login/attachment issues across multiple Atlassian Cloud products.
mitigation_principle: Implement upgrade freeze for non‑critical components; improve scaling isolation; decouple critical components to prevent cascading failures; enforce stricter testing and validation before upgrades

original_source: Unable to access Analytics dashboard (Tableau) in Partner Business Center
symptoms: Inability to access partner portal dashboards embedded in Salesforce
User-facing errors when opening analytics dashboard
failure_pattern: The Tableau dashboard service, embedded within Salesforce, experienced an outage that prevented users from accessing analytics dashboards. The failure propagated to the partner portal, causing a critical outage for all users attempting to view dashboards.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated health checks for third‑party services; add circuit breaker and fallback UI; increase monitoring and alerting granularity; maintain redundancy or local caching; document and test recovery procedures

failure_pattern: A misconfigured rate limit in an internal authentication service caused excessive 429 responses, triggering client retries that multiplied load and cascaded failures across dependent services, leading to widespread authentication and user profile disruptions.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated rate limit configuration validation; enforce client retry/backoff policies; perform dependency graph analysis to reduce cascading failures; conduct regular load testing of inter-service interactions; monitor retry behavior and rate limits

original_source: Issue in reactivating paid apps after it has been suspended due to non-payment, after making the payment
failure_pattern: When a paid app is suspended for non-payment, an administrator uninstalls and reinstalls it, then pays; the reinstall path fails to clear the suspended state, so the reactivation logic does not activate the app, leaving it permanently suspended.
mitigation_principle: Ensure reinstall clears suspension state; make reactivation logic idempotent; add automated tests for reinstall after suspension; monitor reactivation status; provide support fallback for manual restoration

failure_pattern: A temporary outage of Atlassian Partner products caused the Partner Support Portal to become unavailable, resulting in service disruptions for users.
mitigation_principle: Implement health checks and automated failover for third‑party services; add circuit breaker patterns; monitor third‑party API latency and error rates; set up alerting for service degradation; perform regular dependency audits.

original_source: Management of Apps is partially unavailable on different platforms
symptoms: intermittent failures in app lifecycle operations
failure_pattern: A misconfiguration in the Forge app management backend caused the service to reject lifecycle operations, leading to partial unavailability of app installation, removal, and deployment across multiple Atlassian platforms, including the developer console and tunneling features.
mitigation_principle: Implement automated configuration validation and testing before deployment; use feature flags for gradual rollouts; add health checks and circuit breakers; monitor service metrics and set alerts; maintain a rollback plan; enforce code review for configuration changes.

symptoms: customers unable to create support tickets
failure_pattern: An outage at AWS disrupted Atlassian's cloud services, causing widespread service unavailability and preventing support ticket creation. Atlassian teams monitored the situation, communicated updates, and coordinated with AWS until the issue was resolved, after which services gradually recovered.
mitigation_principle: Implement multi-cloud or hybrid redundancy; set up automated health checks for third‑party services; maintain clear incident communication protocols; establish fallback support channels; conduct regular incident response drills
